title: 1 Chronicles Chapter 2 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 1 Chronicles chapter 2 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 1 Chronicles Chapter 2 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 1 Chronicles Chapter 2.

questions.question: Who were the first three sons of Judah mentioned in 1 Chronicles 2?
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 2:3 states that the sons of Judah were Er, Onan, and Shelah.

questions.question: According to 1 Chronicles 2, who was the father of Pharez and Zerah?
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 2:4 mentions that Tamar, Judah's daughter-in-law, bore him Pharez and Zerah.

questions.question: How many sons of Israel are listed in 1 Chronicles 2:1-2?
questions.explanation: Verses 1 and 2 list the twelve sons of Israel: Reuben, Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, Zebulun, Dan, Joseph, Benjamin, Naphtali, Gad, and Asher.

questions.question: Who was called 'the troubler of Israel' in 1 Chronicles 2?
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 2:7 identifies Achar, son of Carmi, as the troubler of Israel who transgressed in the accursed thing.

questions.question: Who was the prince of the children of Judah mentioned in 1 Chronicles 2?
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 2:10 states that Nahshon was prince of the children of Judah.

questions.question: According to 1 Chronicles 2, who was the seventh son of Jesse?
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 2:15 states that David was the seventh son of Jesse.

questions.question: True or False: Er, the firstborn of Judah, was evil in the sight of the LORD and was slain by God.
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 2:3 confirms that Er was evil in the sight of the LORD and He slew him.

questions.question: Who was the father of Amasa according to 1 Chronicles 2?
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 2:17 states that Abigail bore Amasa and that Jether the Ishmeelite was his father.

questions.question: Which of the following was NOT a son of Pharez in 1 Chronicles 2?
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 2:5 lists Hezron and Hamul as sons of Pharez; Zimri was a son of Zerah (1 Chronicles 2:6), and Jerahmeel was a son of Hezron (1 Chronicles 2:9).

questions.question: Who was the wife of Caleb that bore Jesher, Shobab, and Ardon?
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 2:18 states that Azubah was Caleb's wife and bore Jesher, Shobab, and Ardon.

questions.question: True or False: Caleb had a son named Hur by his wife Ephrath.
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 2:19 confirms that after Azubah died, Caleb took Ephrath who bore him Hur.

questions.question: Who were the sisters of David mentioned in 1 Chronicles 2?
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 2:16 states that David's sisters were Zeruiah and Abigail.

questions.question: Which son of Zerah is NOT listed in 1 Chronicles 2:6?
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 2:6 lists Zimri, Ethan, Heman, Calcol, and Dara as sons of Zerah. Azariah was a son of Ethan (1 Chronicles 2:8).

questions.question: True or False: Nahshon begat Salma, who begat Boaz, according to 1 Chronicles 2.
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 2:11 states that Nahshon begat Salma, and Salma begat Boaz.

questions.question: In 1 Chronicles 2, which of these comes first in the genealogy?
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 2:10 shows Ram begat Amminadab; Amminadab begat Nahshon; Nahshon begat Salma; and Salma begat Boaz, so Ram comes first.

medium.title: 1 Chronicles Chapter 2 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 1 Chronicles Chapter 2 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to 1 Chronicles 2, who was born to Hezron after he married the daughter of Machir at the age of sixty?
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 2:21 states that Hezron married the daughter of Machir when he was sixty and she bore him Segub. This shows the continuation of Hezron's lineage through this marriage.

questions.question: How many cities did Jair, the son of Segub, have in the land of Gilead?
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 2:22 clearly states that Jair had twenty-three cities in the land of Gilead, indicating his prominence and territorial holdings.

questions.question: What additional territories did Jair take over, as mentioned in 1 Chronicles 2?
questions.explanation: According to 1 Chronicles 2:23, Jair took Geshur, Aram, and Kenath along with the towns of Jair. This expands the understanding of his influence beyond just Gilead.

questions.question: True or False: After Hezron died, his wife Abiah bore him Ashur, the father of Tekoa.
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 2:24 states that after Hezron died, his wife Abiah bore Ashur, who was the father of Tekoa, showing lineage continuation after Hezron's death.

questions.question: Who was the firstborn of Jerahmeel, the firstborn of Hezron?
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 2:25 identifies Ram as the firstborn of Jerahmeel, who in turn was the firstborn of Hezron, indicating the primary heir in this family line.

questions.question: What was the name of Jerahmeel's wife who was the mother of Onam?
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 2:26 reveals that Jerahmeel had another wife named Atarah, who was the mother of Onam, highlighting the family relationships.

questions.question: Which of the following was NOT a son of Ram, the firstborn of Jerahmeel?
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 2:27 lists Maaz, Jamin, and Eker as the sons of Ram. Shammai is mentioned later as a son of Onam, not Ram.

questions.question: Who were the sons of Onam, brother of Shammai?
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 2:28 states that Onam's sons were Shammai and Jada, showing the family structure within Jerahmeel's descendants.

questions.question: True or False: Seled, son of Nadab, died without children.
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 2:30 explicitly states that Seled died without children, which is important in the context of inheritance and lineage.

questions.question: Who was given Sheshan's daughter in marriage, according to 1 Chronicles 2?
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 2:34-35 explain that Sheshan had no sons but daughters, so he gave his daughter to Jarha, his Egyptian servant, to wife, continuing the family line.

questions.question: Which sequence correctly follows the genealogy starting with Attai?
options: Attai begat Nathan, Nathan begat Zabad, Zabad begat Ephlal
Attai begat Zabad, Zabad begat Nathan, Nathan begat Ephlal
Nathan begat Attai, Attai begat Zabad, Zabad begat Ephlal
Zabad begat Attai, Attai begat Nathan, Nathan begat Ephlal
questions.correctAnswer: Attai begat Nathan, Nathan begat Zabad, Zabad begat Ephlal
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 2:36-37 outlines this genealogy clearly with Attai as father of Nathan, Nathan father of Zabad, and Zabad father of Ephlal.

questions.question: What does the passage about Sheshan giving his daughter to his servant teach us about faith and family responsibility?
options: Faith and family responsibilities sometimes require unconventional actions to preserve lineage.
Only blood relations can continue the family name.
Servants cannot be trusted with family matters.
Marriage outside the tribe is forbidden.
questions.correctAnswer: Faith and family responsibilities sometimes require unconventional actions to preserve lineage.
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 2:34-35 shows that Sheshan gave his daughter to his servant to maintain family lineage, teaching flexibility and responsibility in faith and family matters.

questions.question: Who was the father of Tekoa according to 1 Chronicles 2?
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 2:24 states that Ashur, born to Abiah after Hezron's death, was the father of Tekoa, marking the origin of this important lineage.

questions.question: True or False: Jether, son of Jada, died without children.
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 2:32 says Jether died without children, but the question incorrectly associates Jether as son of Jada; Jether was son of Jada, so the statement is true. However, the question tests attention to detail on relationship and death without offspring.

questions.question: Which of these lists correctly identifies the sons of Jonathan, son of Jada?
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 2:33 states that Jonathan's sons were Peleth and Zaza, clarifying the family branches of Jerahmeel.

hard.title: 1 Chronicles Chapter 2 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 1 Chronicles Chapter 2.

questions.question: Who was the father of Bethzur according to 1 Chronicles 2?
questions.explanation: Verse 1 Chronicles 2:45 states that Maon was the father of Bethzur, and he was the son of Shammai.

questions.question: Which son of Caleb's concubine Ephah is mentioned as having a son named Gazez?
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 2:46 mentions that Haran, son of Ephah, begat Gazez, indicating the genealogical line.

questions.question: How many cities did Jair have in the land of Gilead?
questions.explanation: According to 1 Chronicles 2:22, Jair had twenty-three cities in the land of Gilead.

questions.question: Which family is identified as coming from Hemath, the father of the house of Rechab?
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 2:55 specifies that the Kenites came from Hemath, the father of the house of Rechab.

questions.question: Which daughter of Caleb is mentioned in 1 Chronicles 2?
questions.explanation: Verse 1 Chronicles 2:49 identifies Achsah as the daughter of Caleb.

questions.question: What is the significance of the name 'Achar' mentioned in 1 Chronicles 2:7?
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 2:7 calls Achar 'the troubler of Israel' who transgressed the thing accursed, indicating his negative role.

questions.question: Who was the father of Boaz, according to the genealogy in 1 Chronicles 2?
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 2:11 states that Nahshon begat Salma, and Salma begat Boaz.

questions.question: Which literary device is predominantly used in 1 Chronicles 2 to present the genealogies?
questions.explanation: The chapter uses genealogical parallelism by listing descendants in parallel family lines to emphasize lineage connections, as seen throughout 1 Chronicles 2.

questions.question: The Hebrew name 'Pharez' means what, which foreshadows a key biblical theme?
questions.explanation: Pharez means 'breakthrough' in Hebrew, as found in 1 Chronicles 2:4. This name foreshadows the Messianic lineage breakthrough through Judah, fulfilled in Jesus (Matthew 1:3).

questions.question: Which other Old Testament passage echoes the theme of the genealogical lineage of Judah found in 1 Chronicles 2?
questions.explanation: Genesis 49:10 prophesies the coming ruler from the tribe of Judah, connecting directly with the genealogical emphasis on Judah's descendants in 1 Chronicles 2.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage fulfills the Messianic lineage traced in 1 Chronicles 2 through David?
questions.explanation: Matthew 1:6-16 provides the genealogy of Jesus, tracing His lineage through David and Judah, fulfilling the genealogical record in 1 Chronicles 2:15-16.

questions.question: Which verse indicates that Sheshan had no sons but gave his daughter to his servant, an Egyptian named Jarha?
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 2:34 states that Sheshan had no sons but daughters and gave one to his servant Jarha as wife.

questions.question: True or False: The families of scribes who dwelt at Jabez are identified as Kenites in 1 Chronicles 2.
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 2:55 identifies the families of scribes at Jabez as Kenites, descendants of Hemath, father of the house of Rechab.

questions.question: True or False: Nahshon was the father of Amminadab and was a prince of the children of Judah.
questions.explanation: According to 1 Chronicles 2:10, Nahshon begat Amminadab and was prince of the children of Judah.

questions.question: Who is identified as the father of the city Kirjathjearim's inhabitants in 1 Chronicles 2?
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 2:50-52 identifies Shobal as the father of Kirjathjearim and its descendants.

theological.title: 1 Chronicles Chapter 2 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 1 Chronicles Chapter 2 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What theological doctrine is illustrated by the death of Er, Judah's firstborn, as described in 1 Chronicles 2:3?
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 2:3 states that Er was evil in the sight of the LORD and God slew him, demonstrating God's righteous judgment against sin.

questions.question: Which characteristic of God is demonstrated by the lineage preservation through Tamar bearing Pharez and Zerah, despite family failures?
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 2:4 shows Tamar bearing Pharez and Zerah, continuing the lineage, indicating God's sovereign control in fulfilling His purposes despite human failings.

questions.question: What doctrinal teaching can be drawn from the repeated mention of lineages and genealogies in 1 Chronicles 2:5-6?
options: God's covenant faithfulness to His people
questions.correctAnswer: God's covenant faithfulness to His people
questions.explanation: Verses 5-6 emphasize the detailed genealogy of Judah's descendants, illustrating God's ongoing covenant faithfulness through generations.

questions.question: In 1 Chronicles 2:7, Achar is called 'the troubler of Israel.' What does this reveal about the nature of sin in the community of God's people?
options: Sin disrupts the holiness and unity of God's people
Sin is easily forgiven without consequences
Sin only affects individuals, not communities
Sin is irrelevant to God's purposes
questions.correctAnswer: Sin disrupts the holiness and unity of God's people
questions.explanation: The label 'troubler of Israel' for Achar in 1 Chronicles 2:7 shows that sin causes disturbance and harm to the community, highlighting its destructive nature.

questions.question: How does the genealogy from Ram to David (1 Chronicles 2:9-15) typologically foreshadow Christ in this chapter?
options: By tracing the royal line culminating in David, the kingly ancestor of Christ
By focusing on prophetic descendants only
questions.correctAnswer: By tracing the royal line culminating in David, the kingly ancestor of Christ
questions.explanation: Verses 9-15 present a genealogy ending with David, from whom Christ is descended, foreshadowing Christ's kingship (Romans 1:3).

questions.question: What attribute of God is demonstrated by His preservation of David’s lineage despite the sinful past of Judah’s family (1 Chronicles 2:16-17)?
questions.explanation: The continuation of David’s lineage through a family with failings (verse 16-17) shows God's grace and mercy in preserving His redemptive plan.

questions.question: What broader biblical narrative connection is emphasized by Caleb’s descendants being described as founders of cities and families in 1 Chronicles 2:18-21?
options: The establishment of God's people in the Promised Land
questions.correctAnswer: The establishment of God's people in the Promised Land
questions.explanation: Caleb’s descendants founding cities (2:18-21) connects to the biblical theme of God's people settling the land promised to Abraham's descendants.

questions.question: Synthesis: How do 1 Chronicles 2:22-23 and 2:24 together illustrate God's providential care in allotting land and families to His people?
options: God divinely assigns territories and ensures family continuity
God leaves land distribution to human chance
God punishes families by land deprivation
God prefers some families over others arbitrarily
questions.correctAnswer: God divinely assigns territories and ensures family continuity
questions.explanation: Verses 22-23 show Jair’s cities in Gilead and 24 shows Hezron’s widow bearing Ashur, indicating God’s providence in both land inheritance and family lines.

questions.question: What doctrinal truth about human mortality and divine promise is reflected in the account of Jerahmeel’s descendants in 1 Chronicles 2:25-33?
options: God sustains His covenant people despite death and childlessness
Human lineage is irrelevant to God
Only the firstborn matters to God
God rejects those with no children
questions.correctAnswer: God sustains His covenant people despite death and childlessness
questions.explanation: The genealogies showing some dying without children (e.g., Nadab and Jether) yet the family continues reveals God’s sustaining covenant (2:25-33).

questions.question: What attribute of God is revealed through Sheshan’s servant Jarha marrying his daughter and starting a line in 1 Chronicles 2:34-35?
questions.explanation: Despite social status differences, God includes Jarha, an Egyptian servant, into the covenant community through marriage (2:34-35), showing providence and inclusiveness.

questions.question: Synthesis: Considering 1 Chronicles 2:36-41 and 2:42-47, how do these genealogies reveal God’s faithfulness in preserving the tribes through successive generations?
options: God maintains His covenant promises through continuous family lines
Genealogies are irrelevant to God’s plan
Families are randomly chosen without purpose
questions.correctAnswer: God maintains His covenant promises through continuous family lines
questions.explanation: The detailed genealogies in these verses demonstrate God's ongoing faithfulness in preserving His people’s lineage across generations.

questions.question: What redemptive narrative connection is found in the mention of Bethlehem as a city founded by Salma in 1 Chronicles 2:51 and 2:54?
options: Bethlehem as the birthplace of the Messiah
Bethlehem as a city of exile
Bethlehem as a place of judgment
Bethlehem as a place of rebellion
questions.correctAnswer: Bethlehem as the birthplace of the Messiah
questions.explanation: The mention of Bethlehem, Salma’s city (2:51, 2:54), ties the genealogy to the Messianic birthplace, connecting to Jesus’ birth narrative (Micah 5:2; Luke 2:4-7).

questions.question: Synthesis: What combined doctrinal insight about God’s providence and human responsibility can be drawn from the genealogies of Caleb’s sons and concubines in 1 Chronicles 2:42-49?
options: God providentially preserves lineage through both legitimate and concubine offspring
Only sons by the primary wife matter to God
God is indifferent to human family structures
questions.correctAnswer: God providentially preserves lineage through both legitimate and concubine offspring
questions.explanation: The inclusion of sons by concubines alongside primary wives' sons (2:42-49) shows God’s providence in sustaining His people’s lineage comprehensively.

questions.question: Apologetics: Sceptics claim genealogies in 1 Chronicles 2 are mere myths without historic value. What does this chapter actually teach about the role of genealogies in Scripture?
options: Genealogies affirm God's covenant faithfulness and historical continuity
questions.correctAnswer: Genealogies affirm God's covenant faithfulness and historical continuity
questions.explanation: This chapter’s genealogies (entire chapter) demonstrate God's faithfulness in preserving His covenant people across generations, providing theological and historical grounding (Luke 3:23-38).

questions.question: What does the mention of the 'families of the scribes which dwelt at Jabez' in 1 Chronicles 2:55 teach about God's provision for His covenant community?
options: God provides for spiritual leadership and preservation of His word
God neglects the role of scribes
questions.correctAnswer: God provides for spiritual leadership and preservation of His word
questions.explanation: The mention of scribes' families (2:55) illustrates God’s provision for spiritual leadership and the preservation of His covenant through Scripture.
